subject: mathematics
question_text: If the matrix with rows (x−1, 2, y−5), (2x, 0, z) and (1, −1, 1+a) equals the matrix with rows (1−x, 2, −y), (2, 0, 2) and (1, −1, 1), then find the values of x, y, z and a.

mark_split.label: Solve for x, y, z and a

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 2(ii), book p.31. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives one mark to turning the matrix equation into separate element equations and one to solving them, because a student who only equates the positions has done the matrix half of the question. This matrix carries a built-in consistency check that the answer uses: position (1,1) gives x − 1 = 1 − x and position (2,1) gives 2x = 2, and both give x = 1. Related card in the same unit: ts_ipe_m1a_mat_vsaq_equality_3x3 is a different 3×3 equality question from another source book, so the two are not duplicates. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find x, y, z and a from this matrix equation.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Equate corresponding elements
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two matrices are equal only when every entry in the same position is equal. Write down only the positions that carry an unknown; the rest are already identical.
steps.memory_tip: Same position, same value. Nine positions here, but only five of them carry an unknown.
lines: Both are 3×3, so equate each position:

recall.must_convey: That equal matrices have equal corresponding entries, which turns the matrix equation into separate element equations.
accept: equal matrices means every corresponding entry is equal so I get separate equations
compare each position and write the equation it gives
match entry by entry and only five positions have unknowns
corresponding elements equate cheste chinna equations vasthai
equate the entries in the same row and column

steps.why: Matrix equality is defined entry by entry: same order, and the same number in every position. That definition is the whole method here.
common_mistakes: Matching entries in the wrong positions.
Skipping the position (2,1) equation, which is the check on x.

steps.label: Solve for x, y, z and a
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Each equation holds one unknown, so each is a one-line solve. y is not a whole number here, and that is correct — do not round it.
steps.memory_tip: Two different positions give x, and both give x = 1. If they disagreed, the equality could not hold.
lines: The entry 2x = 2 gives x = 1 as well.

recall.must_convey: That solving the element equations gives x = 1, y = 5/2, z = 2 and a = 0.
accept: x is one, y is five by two, z is two and a is zero
solve each small equation to get one, five by two, two and zero
both x equations give x equals one, then y is two point five
prathi equation solve cheste x one y five by two z two a zero
the four values are one, five halves, two and zero

steps.why: Every equation here involves a single unknown, so none of them needs the others. That is why this is a 2-mark question and not a simultaneous-equations one.
common_mistakes: Writing y = 5 by reading y − 5 = −y as y − 5 = 0.
Writing a = 1 instead of a = 0 from 1 + a = 1.
